description: NEGATIVE (issue #825): a DEFERRED handler block sees its enclosing scope in FULL, so a read of a name the root scope binds later is not reported. `spec/execution-model.md:401-403` — a binding an enclosing scope creates is visible "to a deferred handler block whenever the handler fires" — and `:423-424` forbids the checker reporting across a scope boundary a name a deferred handler COULD reach, which is the operative word: the handler need only be able to fire after line 2, not to actually do so. Note what the run stage does and does not show here: an `on_click` handler needs host input, so under the harness's empty host it never fires (zero print events) and `execute()` being clean is not evidence either way. The claim this fixture pins is the CHECK stage. The contrasting eager case is tests/conformance/core-language/check/undefined-var-eager-block-reads-a-later-enclosing-binding, which is byte-similar, DOES run at the point it is written, and MUST report — `execute()` raises `ol-undefined-var` on it, measured. A checker that treated the two alike satisfies one fixture and breaks the other, which is the point of shipping them as a pair.
